extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for an NIH R01 (PAR-16-242) / NIAID sample application (investigators preparing/resubmitting federal grant applications)
extracted.subtask_description: A sample/resubmission NIH R01 (Bioengineering Research Grants PAR-16-242) application showing required forms, project summary, facilities/resources, equipment listing, resource sharing and authentication plans, and other compliance elements needed for an NIH grant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The sample may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 conformance and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Note on Section 508 conformance and accessibility for people with disabilities and users of assistive technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples have been reformatted to improve accessibility. If you have trouble accessing content, contact the NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources at deaweb@niaid.nih.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete SF-424(R&R) required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide required SF 424 (R&R) application fields including Type of Submission, Applicant Information (legal name, DUNS, address), Project Director/PI contact information, Project start and end dates, Estimated project funding, and Applicant certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include correct identifiers (Federal Identifier, Application Identifier, Grants.gov Tracking Number), signature of authorized representative, and all contact details; follow OMB form instructions and expiration dates shown on the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application certify to the statements contained in the list of certifications and assurances and agree to comply with resulting terms if an award is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing acknowledges that statements are true, complete, and accurate to the best of the signer's knowledge and warns of penalties for false statements (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001). Include required list of certifications or a URL where it can be obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects involvement declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether human subjects are involved (Yes/No) and if Yes provide exemption status or IRB review/pending/approval details and Human Subject Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If YES, indicate whether the project is exempt from federal regulations and check the appropriate exemption number; indicate IRB approval date or whether IRB review is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals use declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether vertebrate animals are used (Yes/No) and provide IACUC review status, IACUC approval date, and Animal Welfare Assurance Number if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, indicate whether IACUC review is pending and provide IACUC approval date and assurance number as required by the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary/privileged information disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether proprietary or privileged information is included in the application (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit if proprietary information is included so reviewers and administrators can handle appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental impact disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the project has an actual or potential impact (positive or negative) on the environment and whether an exemption, environmental assessment (EA), or environmental impact statement (EIS) has been performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, provide explanation and documentation about environmental review or exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic place designation disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if the research performance site is designated or eligible to be designated as a historic place (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, provide explanation as requested on the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: International activities disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the project involves activities outside the United States or partnerships with international collaborators (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, identify countries and optionally provide explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required application attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach Project Summary/Abstract, Project Narrative, Bibliography & References Cited, Facilities & Other Resources, Equipment, and Other Attachments as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use distinct filenames for attachments (example filenames shown) and ensure each required attachment is present and complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Project Summary/Abstract that states the long-term goal, specific objective, central hypothesis, rationale, approaches to be used, significance, and expected outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample includes: long-term goal to find diagnostic and treatment approaches; objective to determine mechanics/structure of biofilm infections; central hypothesis about spatial structure and mechanics controlling virulence; three specific aims; and statements of significance and broader impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative: Public health relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: A short Project Narrative stating the relevance of the proposed research to public health and how it aligns with the NIH mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the research fosters fundamental discoveries and innovative strategies that ultimately protect health (as in the sample's statement of relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional facilities, laboratory space (size and characteristics), core facility access, computing resources, administrative support, and evidence of institutional commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include square footage, descriptions of microscopy rooms, wet lab facilities, shared equipment, IT support, seminar and meeting spaces, and details of administrative support and startup funds as evidence of a supportive environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major equipment availability and specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: List major equipment available to perform the proposed research, including specific instruments and their capabilities (microscopes, AFM, confocal, rheometer, servers, cameras, temperature-control enclosures, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide instrument models, relevant specs (e.g., camera quantum efficiency, objective magnifications, AFM resolution), whether equipment is shared, and how it will be used to accomplish specific aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to core facilities and services
rubrics_metrics.description: Document availability and scope of institutional core facilities (imaging, sequencing, mass spectrometry, NMR, microscopy cores, genomic sequencing, protein/metabolite analysis, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List individual core services likely to be used, their capabilities (e.g., Imaris, Metamorph software), and policies for access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment and personnel support
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional commitments (startup funds, summer salary support), personnel (postdocs, graduate and undergraduate students), and administrative support available for the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence such as startup package details, allocated summer salary, shared staff, and membership in centers that provide mentoring and seminar series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan — materials (strains)
rubrics_metrics.description: New bacterial strains generated or harvested will be permanently stored (e.g., at -80°C) in replicate and made available to other researchers upon request; strains shipped at requester's expense and according to biosafety protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State storage conditions, shipment policies, and that strains will be provided following BSL-2 shipping protocols if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan — data and software
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication and upon request, share experimental protocols, software developed, microscopy movies, analysis, rheology and AFM data; deposit sequences in public repositories (Short-Read Archive, Pseudomonas Genome Database, Sequence Read Archive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide file formats (open formats like TIFF for images, TXT for analysis), software environments (Matlab, IDL), metadata inclusion, and timelines for deposition (e.g., upon publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management, storage, backup and archival
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain data in both proprietary and open formats on redundant servers, perform regular backups (automated RAID, tape backups, removable drives), and store archival data on stable long-term media with plans to upgrade as technology progresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: doubly-redundant RAID Linux server, off-site tape backups via computing center, open formats (TIFF/TXT), and retention of careful lab notebooks to reconstruct experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship and timely publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and submit for publication promptly and ensure authorship accurately reflects contributions; post-publication, share data and metadata with other researchers upon request at incremental cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify how small files will be shared (email/network transfer) and options for larger datasets (portable media, requester-supplied drives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of strains
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticate bacterial strains using PCR on the respective genes (transposon-disrupted strains show size increase), store strains at -80°C, periodically reisolate and check phenotypic/antibiotic markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe prior use of this authentication approach and cite examples where it verified strain identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of antibodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify antibodies using Western blot and immunoprecipitation with EPS extracts from wild-type, over-expressor, and knockout strains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentation of validation and reference previous successful validation if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication and monitoring of animal models
rubrics_metrics.description: For animal models (e.g., outbred white mice), review vendor health monitoring reports and sentinel animal reports rather than performing separate authentication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document reliance on vendor health data and facility sentinel monitoring as a means of ensuring animal health and suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication and validation of chemicals/reagents
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchase high-quality chemical reagents from reputable suppliers and validate them by checking pH, mass spectrometry, and confirming known biological activity (such as minimal inhibitory concentrations for antibiotics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List suppliers (e.g., Sigma-Aldrich, Invitrogen) and provide procedures for validating key reagents prior to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource availability and sharing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify conditions under which data, protocols, software, and materials will be shared (timing, modes of transfer, costs), and the repositories to be used for sequence and transcriptome data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include email/network transfer for small files, portable media for large files, shipment of strains at requester's expense, and deposition to SRA and genome databases at time of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims and hypothesis statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state the central hypothesis and enumerate specific aims (sample lists three aims: determine spatial structure and mechanics in vivo; determine microenvironment differentiation; determine role in biofilm-neutrophil interactions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie aims to rationale and methods, and explain how completion will identify therapeutic targets and develop broadly-applicable platforms.
